definitions.explanation: The act of fitting one object into another, or the resulting joint or piece. Used in woodworking, jewelry, construction, and crafts for pieces that fit snugly into prepared openings.
In photography, video, and design, the technique of inserting one image or footage into another, such as green-screen compositing or picture-in-picture effects.

notes:
The noun form of ⟦{嵌|は}め{込|こ}む→嵌め込む：06385_hamekomu⟧ (to fit in; to embed). Written variously as {嵌|は}め{込|こ}み, はめ{込|こ}み, or はめこみ. The kanji {嵌|はめ} is not in the standard jouyou kanji list, so kana writing is common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {嵌|は}め{込|こ}み{細工|ざいく}: inlay work; marquetry
- {嵌|は}め{込|こ}み{式|しき}: snap-fit type; insertion-fit type
- {嵌|は}め{込|こ}み⟦{合成|ごうせい}→合成：12027_gousei⟧: composite editing; superimposition
- {嵌|は}め{込|こ}み⟦{映像|えいぞう}→映像：04444_eizou⟧: composited video

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {象嵌|ぞうがん}: inlay (traditional craft term) — specifically refers to metal or precious material inlay in metalwork
- {組|く}み{込|こ}み: built-in; embedded — used more for systems and software
- ⟦{挿入|そうにゅう}→挿入：12828_sounyuu⟧: insertion — more general, not specific to fitting pieces together
